                    ### Question
                    A 28-year-old man presents for a pre-placement health check-up. Auscultation reveals a mid-systolic click. An echocardiogram reveals a floppy mitral valve and a dilated aortic root. An ocular examination finds a subluxated lens superior and laterally. What is the most likely genetic defect?

                    ### Options

opb. Cystathionine synthase deficiency
opc. Fibrillin
opd. Dystrophin
ope. Spectrin

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The most likely genetic defect in this case is a mutation in the Fibrillin gene, associated with Marfan syndrome. The presence of a floppy mitral valve, dilated aortic root, mid-systolic click, and subluxated lens are all consistent with the manifestations of Marfan syndrome, which is linked to mutations in the Fibrillin gene.
